- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- If sentiment shows early positive spikes (e.g., 0.20–0.40), model often overshoots and fails to account for volatility; apply downward correction of 3–8% in first 5–7 days after spike.
- When history shows strong upward trend, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in later days (e.g., 15–30d horizon).
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp drop, model underestimates risk; add 1–3% downward bias for 3–5 days post-drop.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment volatility; use sentiment as proxy for volatility weight.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries, model may be overconfident; apply smoothing or reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to reflect low conviction.
